SIX_HARD_BREAKS.944_claim: SUPP fuses grading and availability, so the coexistence theorem loses its subject; the named zero-available-total boundary becomes vacuous
SIX_HARD_BREAKS.verdict: REPAIRED by scope annotation; 944's claim is narrowed
SIX_HARD_BREAKS.finding: the note's `w` is the graded-constraint v2 grading on the full projection lattice -- a named conditional premise -- NOT the Admissibility distribution. The two objects are not fused by the revision. The zero-available-total boundary stays non-vacuous exactly because `w` may vanish where the Admissibility distribution does not.
SIX_HARD_BREAKS.what_is_now_open: whether `w` and the Admissibility distribution must share a support. If they were identified the boundary WOULD go vacuous; nothing performs that identification.

SIX_HARD_BREAKS.944_claim: two landed classification theorems count rules as set-valued maps; under SUPP the rule space is continuous and both counts cease to be counts of anything; k/64 rests on the finite space
SIX_HARD_BREAKS.finding: the four-subset space and the 3^24/3^24-1 tables are spaces of SUPPORT maps. They remain correct counts of support maps, and k/64 stands as a theorem about the support-level baseline. What is lost is only the claim that this baseline exhausts the axiom's rule content: the distribution refines the support map, so an informative fraction computed on the distribution need not be quantized as k/64. That computation is open and was not performed.

SIX_HARD_BREAKS.944_claim: the witness is explicitly typed on a set-valued static relation; SUPP performs exactly that retyping, so the witness must be re-derived
SIX_HARD_BREAKS.finding: this is stronger than a retyping. The witness needs ONE availability rule to carry both a branch-complete and a singleton-support expansion. With exactly one recorded neighbor the witness rule gives the menu {0,1}, so post-revision both values carry nonzero probability. The singleton-support expansion locks the other value in no continuation, giving it probability zero, hence unavailability -- contradicting the menu {0,1} the same rule asserts. On the locking reading the singleton-support expansion is inadmissible and the independence conclusion FAILS rather than re-scoping.
SIX_HARD_BREAKS.why_contested_not_false: the locking reading is stated in reading note (2), which the memo declares interpretive and non-governing, and is pointed to by section 6 carrying site normalization via 'probability distribution' plus Record's 'locks exactly one'. Under a reading on which the distribution is over something other than the locked possibility, the witness survives. Two readings disagree about a landed conclusion, so this is an owner/audit question.
SIX_HARD_BREAKS.stage_2_effect: the refinement from likelihood to probability distribution NARROWS the escape, because normalization is now explicit in the governing term
SIX_HARD_BREAKS.action_taken: dated CONTESTED bracket added at the section head; no claim, count or conclusion altered; frontmatter claim_scope deliberately untouched

SIX_HARD_BREAKS.944_claim: the theorems derive g.A0 = A0 (set invariance); a distribution requires mu o g = mu, strictly stronger, so the chirality wall and orbit dichotomy must be re-derived
SIX_HARD_BREAKS.verdict: REPAIRED by scope annotation; 944 is right that it is strictly stronger, and right that it under-determines, but no theorem is false
SIX_HARD_BREAKS.finding: every theorem is stated on A0 as a SET and each remains true: the support of a proper-cubic-invariant distribution is a proper-cubic-invariant set. The revision changes two things, both toward strength and neither used by the note: covariance now constrains the distribution itself (mu o g = mu), and consequently the degree-nine wall is a wall on SET-content chirality only -- a cubic-invariant support can carry a non-invariant distribution, so a first-step law can be chiral in its weights while A0 is achiral. The weighted dichotomy, wall, and orientation-bit cost are open.

SIX_HARD_BREAKS.944_claim: a landed Born-form theorem admits zero outcomes as menu members; SUPP makes 'zero-weight member of a menu' a contradiction in terms
SIX_HARD_BREAKS.verdict: DOWNGRADED -- NOT A BREAK. 944's call is over-broad.
SIX_HARD_BREAKS.finding: the menus here are EFFECT PARTITIONS on the explicitly supplied finite carrier E(H_Lambda); a zero outcome is the zero effect carrying w(0)=0 inside a conditional grading surface the note's own N3 scan already records as not derived from the minimal axioms. It is not a probability-zero member of an Admissibility availability menu. The revision retypes the axiom's availability; it does not govern effect-partition conventions in a conditional Born-form bridge.
SIX_HARD_BREAKS.action_taken: a clarifying dated bracket was still added, solely to block the post-adoption misreading that 'zero-weight menu member' has become a contradiction in terms

SIX_HARD_BREAKS.verdict: DEFERRED -- cannot be repaired on this branch
SIX_HARD_BREAKS.blocking_fact: the note does not exist on this branch, is not an ancestor of HEAD, and is NOT on main or origin/main. It was added by commit b4a87e7b8d (2026-08-04) which lives only on the campaign block branches physics-loop/toe-time-blockQ10..Q16-20260802. It is unlanded science.
SIX_HARD_BREAKS.assessment_offered_not_applied: on reading, 944's S6 worry looks over-stated in the same way S5's did. The arena's 164 counterfactual pairs are 'available but unrealized'. Under the revision, available means NONZERO probability, so a counterfactual pair is a positive-probability possibility that was not the one realized -- which is exactly what counterfactual means once the law supplies odds and the realized state supplies the pick. A probability-zero assignment would delete them; availability=support does not. What DOES need saying there is that O2 (which possibility) and O3 (with what weight) are no longer independent open questions in the way the note holds them apart, since the axiom now supplies the distribution.
SIX_HARD_BREAKS.handoff: the S6 annotation must ride with whichever PR lands the cycle-913 note, or be applied immediately after it lands.
